A short series on how to split a sample into groups that look alike. Four
articles, building on each other: the first sets up the distance, the middle two
cover the two classical ways of using it to construct groups, and the last one
covers rerandomization.

All the code is Python, every figure is reproducible from the source, and the
whole thing lives in
[the repository](https://github.com/AlexanderDBolton/BoostSampleSize).

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Series status

*The Mahalanobis distance* and *Rerandomization* are written. *Stratification*
and *Pairwise matching* exist as outlines and are not yet published.
:::
